sprint: Coloring Kit — Crayon, Pastel, and Brush Media for Studio's Doodle Tool
task: The user's own request, delivered with no further elaboration: 'for coloring can we have wax colors , pastel colors and brush and crayons in studio.' Interpreted, disclosed rather than silently guessed and never re-confirmed: 'wax colors' and 'crayons' are treated as one and the same medium (crayons are wax-based), giving exactly 3 distinct drawing media -- Crayon, Pastel, Brush -- each with its own curated 8-colour palette and its own distinct stroke-rendering algorithm, replacing Studio's Doodle tool's single flat pen-colour/thickness picker. Every stroke in st.strokes now optionally carries medium: undefined|'crayon'|'pastel'|'brush' -- absent (every pre-feature stroke) always renders through the exact original, byte-identical algorithm. Three genuinely distinct rendering algorithms, hand-mirrored between js/cardDesigner.js's live editing pad and renderer/slideRenderer.js's real Reader-facing/Publish-facing renderer: Crayon is three offset partially-transparent passes simulating textured wax; Pastel is a single stroke with shadowBlur glow at reduced opacity simulating soft chalk; Brush varies lineWidth continuously along the stroke via a new taper easing function, narrow at the start/end, full width in the middle, simulating a real brush stroke. New medium-switcher UI (3 pill buttons above the pen-tools row) rebuilds the swatch palette and resets the active colour whenever medium changes. Verified via a new 22-assertion Playwright suite split into direct render-path pixel checks (confirming genuine width taper via off-centreline sampling, since a stroke's own centreline is fully painted regardless of width) and a real-UI boot-to-Workspace flow (confirming the medium switcher, palette swaps, and committed-stroke medium all work end to end). Full regression across 6 existing scratch suites sharing renderer/slideRenderer.js's broader render pipeline (84 assertions, 0 failures) plus both goldenBuild.js suites (World Builder v1 and v2), both untouched by this change. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to js/cardDesigner.js, renderer/slideRenderer.js, and css/style.css.
